question: What is the primary purpose of performing a venepuncture?

options.A: To withdraw blood for laboratory tests

explanation: Venepuncture involves puncturing a vein specifically to collect blood samples for diagnostic investigation or therapeutic monitoring. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is proper venepuncture technique crucial in clinical nursing practice?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any hand hygiene steps
options.B: It replaces the need for vital sign monitoring
options.C: It guarantees that intravenous fluids run faster
options.D: It prevents sample hemolysis and reduces patient trauma

explanation: Correct technique safeguards blood sample integrity from damage while minimizing unnecessary pain or injury to the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which vein in the antecubital fossa is usually the first choice for venepuncture?
explanation: The median cubital vein is preferred because it is wide, fixed in position, and less painful to puncture. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: A nurse should exercise caution when accessing the basilic vein because of its proximity to what structure?
explanation: The basilic vein runs close to major nerves and arteries, making accidental arterial puncture or nerve injury more likely if care is not taken. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient had a right-sided mastectomy last year. Where should the nurse collect a blood sample?
explanation: Lymph node removal compromises lymphatic drainage on the affected side, making venepuncture on that arm prone to severe lymphedema and infection. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: What happens if a blood sample is drawn from an arm receiving intravenous fluids?

options.A: The intravenous catheter will become blocked
options.B: The sample will clot too quickly in the vial
options.C: The laboratory results will be falsely diluted
options.D: The patient will experience immediate hemolysis

explanation: Infusing fluids directly mix with local blood flow, altering the concentration of electrolytes and blood components in the sample. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the function of an alcohol swab before venepuncture?

options.A: To remove excess hair from the forearm
options.B: To cleanse and reduce microbial load on the skin
options.C: To dilate the underlying superficial veins
options.D: To numb the puncture site and prevent pain

explanation: Antiseptic swabs reduce skin flora to prevent introducing microorganisms into the bloodstream during needle insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why must a sharps container be placed within arm's reach before starting venepuncture?

options.A: To allow immediate, safe disposal of used needles without recapping
options.B: To comply with local hospital stationery storage rules
options.C: To prevent the blood collection tubes from rolling away
options.D: To keep the patient from seeing the sharp instruments

explanation: Immediate disposal without recapping prevents accidental needle-stick injuries to the healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h4)

question: What action is strictly prohibited after completing a venepuncture procedure?

options.A: Removing gloves before leaving the room
options.B: Labeling the sample tubes at the bedside
options.C: Applying pressure to the puncture site
options.D: Recapping the used needle with two hands

explanation: Two-handed needle recapping is unsafe and frequently leads to accidental skin punctures and blood exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h5)

question: When should hand hygiene be performed during a venepuncture procedure?

options.A: After labeling the specimen tubes in the laboratory
options.B: Before touching the patient and immediately after glove removal
options.C: Only when the nurse's hands have visible dirt on them
options.D: Before putting on a clean lab coat at shift change

explanation: Hand hygiene breaks the chain of infection and must happen before patient contact and after removing protective gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the recommended needle insertion angle for routine venepuncture?
explanation: An angle of 15 to 30 degrees allows successful entry into superficial veins without puncturing through the back wall. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why must the antiseptic skin preparation air-dry before needle insertion?

options.A: To keep the adhesive bandage from slipping off the skin
options.B: To allow the chemical to destroy microbes and prevent burning
options.C: To prevent the blood sample from clotting in the vein
options.D: To make sure the tourniquet stays tight on the arm

explanation: Allowing the alcohol to dry ensures its antimicrobial action is fully active and prevents stinging when the needle enters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: A patient turns pale and complains of dizziness midway through a blood draw. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Stop the procedure and remove the tourniquet and needle
options.B: Apply a tighter tourniquet to maintain arm circulation
options.C: Increase the speed of blood collection into the vacuum tube
options.D: Call the senior doctor immediately without removing the needle

explanation: Fainting indicates a vasovagal reaction; ending the procedure and safeguarding the patient takes immediate priority over sample collection. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h7)

question: What is a localized collection of blood under the skin caused by leaking from a punctured vein called?
explanation: A hematoma develops when blood escapes the blood vessel into surrounding tissue, often recognized by rapid swelling and bruising. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why should patients avoid bending their elbow after venepuncture?

options.A: It prevents the blood in the collection tubes from clotting properly
options.B: It forces air bubbles into the remaining superficial veins
options.C: It causes the intravenous access site to close prematurely
options.D: It increases pressure on the puncture site and causes hematoma formation

explanation: Bending the arm creates a pumping action in the soft tissues, pushing blood out of the vessel wall and forming a bruise. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h8)

question: When should blood collection tubes be labeled with patient details?

options.A: At the nursing station after all patients are done
options.B: At the bedside immediately after collection
options.C: In the laboratory before the samples are spun
options.D: Before entering the patient room for the procedure

explanation: Labeling samples at the bedside prevents misidentification errors and ensures specimen traceability. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h8)
